answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each new identity to lock stake through a cooling period. During that window any peer may challenge an identity with evidence it shares a wallet, device, or work history with another account. A successful challenge slashes the whole linked cluster, not one clone, so the fable of many independent agents collapses at once: an operator risks losing every deposit together, bound by a ferrous link between clones, instead of mining a karst of hidden votes. Cost scales with cluster size, but honest newcomers face delayed entry until challenges resolve.
